facility.name: Kids Zone West
facility.programs_provided: School Age Care,After School Care,Snacks Provided,Drop-In Care,Part Time Care,Transportation to/from School ,Field Trips

provenance.note: Census Geocoder Exact match: 105 WESTERN SKY TRL, JARRELL, TX, 76537

inspection_summary.note: Texas HHSC inspections, report investigations and assessments since October 2017, updated daily.

occurrences.finding: Screen Time Activities - Not Used for Under Two: Observed children under two years old watching Ms Rachel. This was corrected when the tablet was turned off.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Screen Time Activities - Not Used for Under Two (26 TAC §746.2207(a))

occurrences.finding: Infant Care Area Furnishings and Equipment -Use of Safety Straps: Observed 5 infants sitting in the highchair table without safety straps being used. The safety straps were missing. The operation will be ordering straps for the chairs.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Infant Care Area Furnishings and Equipment -Use of Safety Straps (26 TAC §746.2407)

occurrences.finding: Adequate Lighting During Naptime: There was a classroom that had the lights off and a curtain covering the window which made the room too dark. None of the infants could be seen and one of the caregivers could not be seen when licensing walked into the classroom. This was corrected when the caregivers were asked to open the curtain to let in some light.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Adequate Lighting During Naptime (26 TAC §746.2911)

occurrences.finding: Requirements for Feeding Infants-Hold through 6-months: Observed a caregiver holding a bottle to the infants mouth as the infant laid on the floor.  The infant was under 6 months old. This was corrected when the teacher was asked to pick the infant up to feed.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Requirements for Feeding Infants-Hold through 6-months (26 TAC §746.2419(1))

occurrences.finding: Personal use of electronic devices, such as cell phones, MP3 players, tablets, and video games: A caregiver was observed during the walk though of the classrooms to be on their phones watching TiK Tok video's. This was corrected when the caregiver was asked to not be on their phones while supervising caregivers.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Personal use of electronic devices, such as cell phones, MP3 players, tablets, and video games (26 TAC §746.1203(3)(D))

occurrences.finding: Requirements for Feeding Infants - Label Bottles/Cups: During an investigation it was found that a bottle was not labled and was fed to a child in care. This has been corrected and all bottles are now labeled.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Requirements for Feeding Infants - Label Bottles/Cups (26 TAC §746.2419(6))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: During an investigation it was found that a caregiver labeled a bottle with the wrong name which was later sent home to the wrong family and fed to another infant.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment: Observed a fence board missing on the playground that is large enough to allow a child to leave the playground.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)

occurrences.finding: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment: Observed water pipes that are exposed on the playground which can be a tripping hazard.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)

occurrences.finding: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children: Observed lysol and frebreeze in an cabinet with a broken lock that was in reach of the children in the classroom. This was corrected when the chemicals were removed from the unlocked cabinet and placed in a locked cabinet.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children (26 TAC §746.3407(12))

occurrences.finding: Requirements for Feeding Infants-Hold through 6-months: Observed a caregiver hold a bottle to an infants mouth while the infant was propped up on a boppy pillow on the floor next to the caregiver. The caregiver stated that the child could not hold their own bottle. I explained that an infant who cannot hold their own bottle and sit unnassisted should be held to be fed. The infant was picked up by the caregiver.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Requirements for Feeding Infants-Hold through 6-months (26 TAC §746.2419(1))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Using Harsh, Abusive or Profane Language: It was observed on video, a caregiver cursing in front of the children in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling (26 TAC §746.2805(6))

occurrences.finding: Personal use of electronic devices, such as cell phones, MP3 players, tablets, and video games: There was evidence to support that caregivers use their phones while caring for children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Personal use of electronic devices, such as cell phones, MP3 players, tablets, and video games (26 TAC §746.1203(3)(D))

occurrences.finding: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment: Observed a metal vent screen that is broken and falls frequently due to not being ablt to be secured with the latches. One latch is bent and the other latch is missing.   There is also a wooden board  broken in half from the fence on the playground.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know number of children responsible for: Observed one classroom caregiver state that they had 9 chidlren in care but there were only 7 children in the classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know number of children responsible for (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Reporting Suspected Abuse, Neglect, Exploitation-May not delegate responsibility to report: There was an allegation of prohibited punishments being used and it was not reported.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Reporting Suspected Abuse, Neglect, Exploitation-May not delegate responsibility to report (26 TAC §746.201(5))

occurrences.finding: Director Responsibilities - Employee Assignments: During an investigation it was found that multiple reports had been told to the director about a caregiver using prohibited punishments, and the caregiver was not removed from the class.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director Responsibilities - Employee Assignments (26 TAC §746.1003(3))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling: During an investigation, there was enough evidence to support that caregivers are yelling at children as a form of discipline.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling (26 TAC §746.2805(5))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Corporal Punishment: During an investigation it was found that prohibited punishments were being used at the operation.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Corporal Punishment (26 TAC §746.2805(1))

occurrences.finding: Annual Sanitation Inspection: The operation did not have a current sanitation inspection. The last sanitation inspection was completed on 1/23/23. The operation will be scheduling the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Annual Sanitation Inspection (26 TAC §746.3401(a))

occurrences.finding: Basic Requirements for Infants - Free from Choking Objects That May Cause Choking in Infants or Toddlers: Observed pecans on the infant/toddler playground. I observed 2 infants with pecans in their mouths which can be a choking hazard. I spoke with the director regarding picking up the pecans prior to allowing the young infants/toddlers on the playground.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Basic Requirements for Infants - Free from Choking Objects That May Cause Choking in Infants or Toddlers (26 TAC §746.2401(6))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know number of children responsible for: Observed a classroom, the caregivers stated that they had 13 children, but there was 14 children in the room.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know number of children responsible for (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Placement of Groups - Not Exceed Room Capacity: During the inspection it was observed that an outdoor area was over space capacity by 6 children and an indoor classroom was over capacity by 2 children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Placement of Groups - Not Exceed Room Capacity (26 TAC §746.1505(3))

occurrences.finding: Child Becomes Ill in Care - Keep Apart from Others: During the investigation it was found that ill children have been cared for around other children, increasing the chances of spreading illnesses around.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child Becomes Ill in Care - Keep Apart from Others (26 TAC §746.3605(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: During the investigation it was found that there were multiple incidents where children were biting, hitting, kicking, choking, and pushing other children in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Illness Preventing Care - Communicable Disease: During the inspection it was found that children were allowed back into care before the were cleared from a physican to be present.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Illness Preventing Care - Communicable Disease (26 TAC §746.3601(4))

occurrences.finding: Diaper Changing Equipment - Smooth, Non-absorbent, Easy to Clean Surface: During a DFPS investigation, a changing pad was observed to have multiple tears making it absorbent. This was corrected when the torn changing pad was replaced with a new intact changing pad.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Diaper Changing Equipment - Smooth, Non-absorbent, Easy to Clean Surface (26 TAC §746.3503(a))

occurrences.finding: Floors, ceilings and Walls in Good Repair and Clean: During a DFPS investigation, the walls in the classroom were observed to have peeling paint in multiple places.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Floors, ceilings and Walls in Good Repair and Clean (26 TAC §746.3407(9))

occurrences.finding: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months: The last fire inspection available for review was conducted in 2021.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months (26 TAC §746.5101(a))

occurrences.finding: Children's Records Maintained: There were 2 children records out of 10 with outdated immunizations. This was discused with the operations office staff.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records Maintained (26 TAC §746.603(a))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Free of other activities: Observed one caregiver on their phone while caring for children. Observed another caregiver with their phone on their lap. This was corrected when the caregivers quickly put the phones away when licensing entered the room.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Free of other activities (26 TAC §746.1203(6))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know Children's Names and Ages: Observed two classrooms that the caregiver did not know the ages of the children or how many children they had in their care. This was corrected when licensing spoke to both caregivers explaining the importance of knowing this information.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know Children's Names and Ages (26 TAC §746.1203(3))
